verdict: One GB300 prefills Qwen3.8-Flash-Next NVFP4 at 42-47k tok/s single-stream from 16k to 128k input (128k prompt: TTFT 2.8 s) and saturates at ~52-55k tok/s aggregate. Against the GB10 pod on identical prompts that is 11.8-14.8x TP4 and 13.3-16.6x TP2 at 16k-128k input (2.9-5.0x at 1k-4k, where fixed overhead dominates); TP8 had not finished when this file was written. Prefill is compute-bound, as expected: NVIDIA rates the Station at 20 PFLOPS FP4 (15 dense) against roughly 1 PFLOP FP4 per Spark.

config.hardware: NVIDIA GB300 Station (MSI XpertStation WS300), 1x GB300 sm_103, 256,703 MiB HBM3e; Grace 72c; 496 GB LPDDR5X
config.image: vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-aarch64, image id sha256:8e138f4eac3a (vLLM 0.29.1rc1.dev573+ge97573215, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, torch 2.13.0+cu130). NGC 26.08 cannot load qwen4_exp.
config.checkpoint: RadixArk/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, local gb300-station:~/models/qwen38-flashnext-nvfp4-radixark (same checkpoint as the earlier gb300-station and GB10 runs)
config.launcher: gb300-station:~/serve-qwen38.sh 0.92 -> vllm serve --tensor-parallel-size 1 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 64 --enable-chunked-prefill --enable-prefix-caching --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --kv-cache-dtype auto (bf16). max_num_batched_tokens defaulted to 16384. Env TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a FLASHINFER_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=10.3a CUTE_DSL_ARCH=sm_103a.
config.kv_cache_dtype: bf16 (auto). fp8 KV is rejected on sm_103 by FlashAttention; not attempted.
config.prefix_caching: ENABLED on the server, defeated by prompt construction: each request starts with a unique 'Document <uid>' header (harness method), and the server's prefix_cache_hits_total delta is recorded per row: 0 hit tokens in every prefill, RAG and capacity row. Hybrid-model KV cache groups are [1568,1568,1568,1568,4,1568] tokens per block.
config.harness: scripts/llm-prefill-bench.py (the pod agent's harness, unchanged; same CORPUS_SEED 20260924 and RUN_SEED, corpus token sha256 e6f98181... identical to the pod files, so the prompts are byte-for-byte the same token ids). Phases: gate; prefill (lengths 1024,4096,16384,65536,131040; conc 1,4,8; 3 reps at c1; max_tokens 32); rag (8192 in, 256 out, conc 1,2,4,8,16,32, closed loop 3 rounds); capacity_32k (conc 1,4,8,16,24,32,40,48,64); capacity_128k (conc 1,2,4,8,16,24,32); all max_tokens 256 for capacity, ignore_eos, temperature 0, thinking off. Prefill tok/s = usage.prompt_tokens / TTFT (server-reported prompt tokens).
config.derived_max_concurrency_at_32768: about 175 by the same arithmetic (5,747,436 / 32,768); vLLM only prints the max_model_len figure. max_num_seqs 64 is the real admission cap in this config.

summary.note_1024_c4: The 1024-token c4 burst in the main run read 2877.6 tok/s (TTFT 1.42 s), a cold-start outlier (first batch of that shape). A recheck right after the suite (phase prefill_1024_c4_recheck, same four prompts; no prefix-cache hit is possible because this hybrid model's cache block is 1568 tokens, and the hit counter read 0) gave 15428.0 / 15900.8 / 15701.9 tok/s. Use the recheck.

long_context_capacity.memory: KV is not the limit: at 64 x 32k users peak KV use was 41%, and at 32 x 128k users 70%, with 0 preemptions. Every burst was admitted at once (peak_running = N).
long_context_capacity.what_limits: Prefill compute. It is serialized at ~52-55k tok/s aggregate, so a simultaneous burst of N users at context C finishes its last first-token at about N x C / 55k s, and decode for the already-started users slows while later prompts prefill.
long_context_capacity.32k_users: TTFT p95 <= 5 s up to 8 simultaneous users, 9.4 s at 16, 18.3 s at 32, 36.3 s at 64 (all served, no preemption).
long_context_capacity.128k_users: TTFT 2.8 s for 1 user, p95 5.2 s at 2, 9.9 s at 4, 19.4 s at 8, 38.4 s at 16, 76.2 s at 32 (all served, no preemption).

prompt_construction.tail_instruction: In one sentence, what is this document about?

rows.q: What is the capital of France? Answer in one word.
What is 17*23? Answer with the number only.
List the first five prime numbers, comma separated.
In one sentence, what does a network firewall do?
rows.answer: A network firewall acts as a security barrier that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic based on predetermined security rules to prevent unauthorized access.

rag.mode: closed loop: N workers start together, each sends rounds_per_worker requests back to back

capacity_32k.mode: burst: N users each send one unique context-sized request at the same instant

capacity_128k.mode: burst: N users each send one unique context-sized request at the same instant
